slides.title: Drone work in ATAK
slides.html: OpenDefence UAVOps is OpenDefence's drone operations plugin. It takes a soldier's request for a drone to the team that flies it, and brings the result back.

slides.title: From ask to result
slides.html: A forward observer asks for a strike or recon. The headquarters (HQ) or a platoon's tactical operations centre (TOC) assigns a team, or it goes straight to the teams asked.

slides.title: Follow it in the Inbox
slides.html: The asker follows each step in OpenDefence Main's Inbox under Sent. Here the strike on Bunker reads Hit.

slides.title: See drones fly
slides.html: Missions shows which drones fly now and how far each target is from you.

slides.title: It does not fly the drone
slides.html: OpenDefence UAVOps does not fly drones. The drone team records the take-off, the landing and the result, here Hit.

slides.title: The drone on the map
slides.html: The drone shows on the map from the position it already sends, here KOIRA11, or as a marker the team moves By hand.

slides.title: Opens from Drones
slides.html: OpenDefence UAVOps works with OpenDefence Main. It opens from Drones on the thumb bar, the buttons at the bottom left of the map.

slides.title: Needs Data Sync
slides.html: OpenDefence UAVOps also needs the Data Sync plugin, which carries the missions from phone to phone. Without it, Settings warns No Data Sync plugin: missions cannot be sent.

slides.title: Where to start
slides.html: Concepts explains the words used here, and Starting as a user sets your role and unit. Then each role has its own chapter.
